explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares both Multi-Agent Framework and Adversarial Framework LLM evaluations with human judgments on the same set of instances, reporting agreement rates and discussing alignment

prompts.notes: Detailed prompts shown through figures demonstrating positive and negative agent evaluations with specific rubric criteria

guidelines.notes: Five-dimensional rubric with discrete scoring (1-3 points per dimension), weights, and binary classification threshold clearly described

sample_size.notes: Evaluation set of 2,000 query-response pairs used for both automated and human evaluations

quantitative_scores.notes: Agreement rates ranging from 80% to 87% across evaluated models

validation_results.summary_finding: Both LLM evaluation frameworks show strong agreement with human judgments (70-87%), with Multi-Agent Framework achieving higher alignment, demonstrating effective approximation of human evaluation.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM and human evaluations use identical five-dimensional criteria with same rubric weights and scoring system
